proofs.proof_tex:
Fix projected pilots \((\bar\pi,\bar\mu)\).  By their projection sets in \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}higher\text{-}order\text{-}learner}\),
\[
 \kappa\le\bar\pi(x)\le1-\kappa,
 \qquad 0\le\bar\mu(x)\le1.
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}outcomes}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}consistency}\), every observed record in the model has \(0\le y\le1\).  Hence all scalar residuals occurring in \(L\) and \(H\) have absolute value at most one.  The basis bounds in the corrected construction and \(K_h\le h^{-d}\) therefore give constants \(c_L,c_H<\infty\), depending only on \((d,\kappa,\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\) and the fixed normalizations, for which
\[
 \Lambda_L\le c_Lh^{-d},
 \qquad
 \Lambda_H\le c_Hkh^{-2d}.
\]
Indeed, every linear entry contains one factor \(K_h\), at most two fixed-dimensional factors \(\rho_h\), and bounded scalar residuals.  Every quadratic entry additionally contains
\[
 |b_{h,k}(x)^{\mathsf T}b_{h,k}(x')|
 \le \lVert b_{h,k}(x)\rVert_2\lVert b_{h,k}(x')\rVert_2
 \le c_b^2kh^{-d}.
\]

Suppose two main-block samples differ only at index \(r\).  The linear average changes by at most \(2\Lambda_L/m\).  In the ordered quadratic average exactly \(2(m-1)\) summands have \(r\) as one of their two indices, and each old summand differs from its replacement by at most \(2\Lambda_H\).  Consequently
\[
 \lVert T_*(D_*)-T_*(D_*')\rVert_2
 \le {2\Lambda_L\over m}
     +{2(m-1)\,2\Lambda_H\over m(m-1)}
 ={2\Lambda_L+4\Lambda_H\over m}
 \le {C_\Delta\over m}\{h^{-d}+kh^{-2d}\},
\]
where one may take \(C_\Delta=\max\{2c_L,4c_H\}\).  This is deterministic conditional on the pilots and therefore uniform over \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).

The definitions of \(\Delta_\pi\) and \(\Delta_\mu\) are the exact replacement sensitivities of the two pilot averages, and the preceding display shows that \(\overline\Delta_*\) is a valid sensitivity upper bound for the main statistic.  Since
\[
 c_{\delta_n}=\sqrt{2\log(1.25/\delta_n)}+1
 >\sqrt{2\log(1.25/\delta_n)},
\]
\(\mathrm{lem{:}gaussian\text{-}mechanism\text{-}replacement}\) proves that each of the three conditional block releases is \((\epsilon_n^\circ,\delta_n)\)-differentially private.  Since \(\epsilon_n^\circ\le\epsilon_n\), each is also \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differentially private.

It remains to justify the accountant because the main release uses the private pilots.  Let \(Z_\pi,Z_\mu\) denote the pilot releases and let \(W\) denote the main release.  If adjacent full samples differ in \(D_*\), then the law of \((Z_\pi,Z_\mu)\) is unchanged and, for every fixed pilot realization, the conditional kernel of \(W\) satisfies the \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\) privacy inequality; integration over the common pilot law preserves that inequality.  If the change is in \(D_\pi\), the joint output \((Z_\pi,Z_\mu,W)\), conditional on the unchanged \((D_\mu,D_*)\), is a Markov post-processing of \(Z_\pi\): after \(Z_\pi\) is fixed, the remaining randomness uses no further record from \(D_\pi\).  Integrating the pilot privacy inequality through that Markov kernel again preserves the same \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\) parameters.  The case of a change in \(D_\mu\) is identical.  Thus the joint three-block output obeys adaptive parallel composition with the maximum, rather than the sum, of the three budgets.

Finally, spectral stabilization, matrix inversion, evaluation at \(x_0\), and formation and truncation of \(C_n(h,k)\) use only the private joint output.  Applying the same Markov-kernel argument establishes post-processing invariance and proves privacy of both \(\mathsf M_{h,k,J_\pi,J_\mu}^{\mathrm{DP}}\) and \(C_n(h,k)\).

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(T\) be a deterministic statistic with values in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, and let \(\overline\Delta_2\ge\sup_{D\sim D'}\lVert T(D)-T(D')\rVert_2\).  If \(0<\epsilon_n<1\), \(0<\delta_n<1/2\), \(Z\sim N(0,I)\), and \(c_{\delta_n}>\sqrt{2\log(1.25/\delta_n)}\), then
\[
 T(D)+c_{\delta_n}\overline\Delta_2\epsilon_n^{-1}Z
\]
is replacement \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differentially private.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For replacement-adjacent samples, the explicitly calibrated \(\mathsf M_{h,k,J_\pi,J_\mu}^{\mathrm{DP}}\) and \(C_n(h,k)\) are \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differentially private.  The accountant is adaptive parallel composition across \(D_\pi,D_\mu,D_*\), one joint Gaussian mechanism within each block, and post-processing thereafter.  There is a constant \(C_\Delta\), depending only on \((d,\kappa,\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\) and the fixed basis normalizations, such that, conditional on the projected pilots, the main joint moment statistic has replacement \(\ell_2\)-sensitivity at most
\[
 {C_\Delta\over m}\{h^{-d}+k h^{-2d}\},
\]
uniformly over \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original sensitivity claim refers to unnamed kernels and clipping radii, so it does not determine a statistic whose replacement sensitivity can be evaluated.  The proposed claim is tied to the explicit corrected construction and honestly allows dependence on the smoothness exponents that determine the basis dimensions and sup-norm constants.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
There are constants \(C_B,C_S,C_G\), depending only on \((d,\kappa,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L_\pi,L_\mu,L_\tau)\) and the fixed basis normalizations, such that for every \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), every \(0<h\le r_0\), and every \(1\le k\le m h^d\) with \(m h^d\ge C_S^2\log(8/\eta)\), the projected private pilots satisfy the same H\"older-radius and range restrictions as the primitive nuisances and
\[
 \Pr_Q\!\left\{\left|\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)-\tau_Q(x_0)\right|>
 B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)+G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\right\}\le\eta.
\]
The three displayed summands respectively bound localization plus higher-order nuisance bias, sampling fluctuation of the linear and degenerate terms, and all propagated Gaussian release noise.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Spline approximation and local-polynomial norm constants depend on the smoothness exponents and the fixed basis normalization.  The frozen assertion that the constants depend only on dimension, overlap, and radii is therefore too strong.  This correction changes only constant uniformity, not the law class, envelope, or rate.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every \(0<h\le r_0\), every \(1\le k\le m h^d\) satisfying \(m h^d\ge C_S^2\log(8/\eta)\), and every \(J_\pi,J_\mu\ge1\), the released set \(C_n(h,k)\) is replacement \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differentially private and satisfies

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Use the first \(3m\) observations and split them deterministically into \(D_\pi,D_\mu,D_*\), each of size \(m\); discard the remaining at most two observations.  Put \(\mathcal O_0=\mathcal X\times\{0,1\}\times[0,1]\), and, for \(R>0\), define radial clipping by
\[
 \operatorname{clip}_R(v)=v\min\{1,R/\lVert v\rVert_2\},
 \qquad \operatorname{clip}_R(0)=0.
\]
Fix deterministic tensor-spline bases \(\phi_{\pi,J_\pi}\) and \(\phi_{\mu,J_\mu}\) of orders strictly larger than \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\), respectively.  Let \(\operatorname{svec}\) denote the isometric vectorization of a symmetric matrix, and let
\[
 z_{\pi}(x,a,y)=\operatorname{svec}\{\phi_{\pi,J_\pi}(x)\phi_{\pi,J_\pi}(x)^{\mathsf T}\}
       \mathbin\oplus \phi_{\pi,J_\pi}(x)a,
\]
\[
 z_{\mu}(x,a,y)=\operatorname{svec}\{(1-a)\phi_{\mu,J_\mu}(x)\phi_{\mu,J_\mu}(x)^{\mathsf T}\}
       \mathbin\oplus \phi_{\mu,J_\mu}(x)(1-a)y.
\]
For \(u\in\{\pi,\mu\}\), define the replacement sensitivity
\[
 \Delta_u=\sup_{o,o'\in\mathcal O_0}m^{-1}\lVert z_u(o)-z_u(o')\rVert_2,
 \qquad
 \epsilon_n^\circ=\min\{\epsilon_n,1/2\},
 \qquad
 c_{\delta_n}=\sqrt{2\log(1.25/\delta_n)}+1,
\]
and release from the corresponding pilot block
\[
 \widetilde z_u=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m z_u(O_i)
       +c_{\delta_n}\Delta_u(\epsilon_n^\circ)^{-1}Z_u,
 \qquad Z_u\sim N(0,I),
\]
with the three Gaussian vectors used below mutually independent and independent of \(D_n\).  Reconstruct the symmetric Gram matrix and moment vector from \(\widetilde z_u\), spectrally floor the Gram matrix at \(m^{-1}\), solve its normal equation, and call the resulting spline function \(\widetilde u\).  In \(L^2(\mathcal X)\), project \(\widetilde\pi\) onto the closed convex set
\[
 \mathcal C_\pi=\mathcal H^\alpha(L_\pi;\mathcal X)\cap\{v:\kappa\le v\le1-\kappa\}
\]
and project \(\widetilde\mu\) onto
\[
 \mathcal C_\mu=\mathcal H^\beta(L_\mu;\mathcal X)\cap\{v:0\le v\le1\}.
\]
Write the resulting deterministic measurable projections as \(\bar\pi\) and \(\bar\mu\).  If \(\mathcal C_\pi\) is empty, set \(\bar\pi\equiv1/2\), and if \(\mathcal C_\mu\) is empty, set \(\bar\mu\equiv0\).  For every \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\) the relevant sets are nonempty because they contain the corresponding true nuisances.

For the main block, let
\[
 C_h=x_0+[-h/2,h/2]^d,
 \qquad K_h(x)=h^{-d}{\bf1}_{C_h}(x).
\]
The canonical normalizations of \(\rho_h\) and \(b_{h,k}\) are fixed so that, for constants depending only on \((d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\),
\[
 \sup_{x\in C_h}\lVert\rho_h(x)\rVert_2\le c_\rho,
 \qquad
 \sup_{x\in C_h}\lVert b_{h,k}(x)\rVert_2\le c_b k^{1/2}h^{-d/2},
\]
and \(b_{h,k}=0\) off \(C_h\).  For \(o=(x,a,y)\) and \(o'=(x',a',y')\), put
\[
 L_Q(o)=K_h(x)\rho_h(x)\rho_h(x)^{\mathsf T}a\{a-\bar\pi(x)\},
\]
\[
 L_R(o)=K_h(x)\rho_h(x)\{a-\bar\pi(x)\}\{y-\bar\mu(x)\},
\]
\[
 H_Q^0(o,o')=K_h(x)\rho_h(x)\{a-\bar\pi(x)\}
 b_{h,k}(x)^{\mathsf T}b_{h,k}(x')a'\rho_h(x')^{\mathsf T},
\]
\[
 H_R^0(o,o')=K_h(x)\rho_h(x)\{a-\bar\pi(x)\}
 b_{h,k}(x)^{\mathsf T}b_{h,k}(x')\{y'-\bar\mu(x')\},
\]
and set \(H_Q=H_Q^0\) and \(H_R=H_R^0\).  The ordered \(U\)-statistic below automatically includes both record orientations.
Define the concatenated kernels
\[
 L(o)=\operatorname{vec}\{L_Q(o)\}\mathbin\oplus L_R(o),
 \qquad
 H(o,o')=\operatorname{vec}\{H_Q(o,o')\}\mathbin\oplus H_R(o,o'),
\]
and their deterministic clipping radii
\[
 \mathcal V_\pi=\{p:\kappa\le p\le1-\kappa\},
 \qquad \mathcal V_\mu=\{u:0\le u\le1\},
\]
\[
 \Lambda_L=\sup_{\substack{o\in\mathcal O_0\\(p,u)\in\mathcal V_\pi\times\mathcal V_\mu}}
       \lVert L_{p,u}(o)\rVert_2,
 \qquad
 \Lambda_H=\sup_{\substack{o,o'\in\mathcal O_0\\(p,u)\in\mathcal V_\pi\times\mathcal V_\mu}}
       \lVert H_{p,u}(o,o')\rVert_2.
\]
Conditional on \((\bar\pi,\bar\mu)\), form
\[
 T_*={1\over m}\sum_{i=1}^m\operatorname{clip}_{\Lambda_L}\{L(O_i)\}
 -{1\over m(m-1)}\sum_{i\ne j}\operatorname{clip}_{\Lambda_H}\{H(O_i,O_j)\},
\]
set
\[
 \overline\Delta_*={2\Lambda_L+4\Lambda_H\over m},
 \qquad
 \widetilde T_*=T_*+c_{\delta_n}\overline\Delta_*(\epsilon_n^\circ)^{-1}Z_*,
 \qquad Z_*\sim N(0,I),
\]
and reconstruct \((\widetilde Q,\widetilde R)\) from \(\widetilde T_*\).  Set
\[
 \widehat Q_{\mathrm{DP}}
 =U\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\max\left\{s_j,
 {\kappa(1-\kappa)\over4}\right\}\right)V^{\mathsf T}
 \quad\text{when}\quad
 \widetilde Q=U\operatorname{diag}(s_j)V^{\mathsf T}
\]
is a singular-value decomposition.  Let \(\widehat R_{\mathrm{DP}}=\widetilde R\), and return
\[
 \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)
 =\rho_h(x_0)^{\mathsf T}\widehat Q_{\mathrm{DP}}^{-1}\widehat R_{\mathrm{DP}}.
\]
Each block release uses \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\); all normal-equation solving, metric projection, singular-value flooring, inversion, evaluation, and interval formation are post-processing.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The frozen prose does not define the pilot statistics, higher-order kernels, clipping radii, Gaussian covariances, or replacement sensitivities.  The corrected construction makes the estimator a sample map, uses the score-level quadratic correction that cancels the first-order pilot product, and calibrates every release explicitly.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove the simultaneous finite-sample spline-approximation, Hoeffding-component concentration, inverse-stability, and Gaussian-perturbation inequalities for the corrected explicit learner with the displayed envelope.
open_obligations.obstruction: The conditional population cancellation is now explicit, but the frozen core contains no theorem establishing the required tensor-spline approximation constants or exponential concentration for this localized vector-valued order-two statistic.  Treating the definitions of B, S, and G as those bounds would still assume the crux.
open_obligations.attempted: I replaced the unnamed estimator by explicit pilot, linear-score, quadratic-score, clipping, noise, and stabilization formulas; derived the exact conditional population cancellation; and proved the complete replacement-sensitivity bound.  The surviving analytic work is now isolated to projection approximation and concentration rather than estimator ambiguity.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The corrected construction exposes the exact conditional cancellation that the frozen prose only named.  Fix the projected pilots and write \(g=\pi_Q-\bar\pi\), \(r=\mu_{0,Q}-\bar\mu\).  For a local-polynomial coefficient \(\vartheta\), put \(t_\vartheta=\tau_Q-\rho_h^{\mathsf T}\vartheta\).  Conditional expectation and the definitions of \(\pi_Q,\mu_{0,Q},\tau_Q\) give, pointwise in \(X=x\),
\[
 \mathbb E_Q[(A-\bar\pi)(Y-\bar\mu-A\rho_h^{\mathsf T}\vartheta)\mid X=x]
 =\pi_Q(1-\bar\pi)t_\vartheta+gr.
\]
Since \(\pi_Q(1-\bar\pi)=\pi_Q(1-\pi_Q)+\pi_Qg\), the right side is
\[
 \pi_Q(1-\pi_Q)t_\vartheta+g(r+\pi_Qt_\vartheta).
\]
Let \(\Pi_k\) be the componentwise \(L^2(C_h)\)-projection onto the span of \(b_{h,k}\).  Independence of the two records in the order-two kernel and orthonormality of \(b_{h,k}\) imply that its conditional population contribution equals the inner product of the two projected factors.  Therefore the population corrected score is exactly
\[
 \int_{C_h}K_h\rho_h\pi_Q(1-\pi_Q)t_\vartheta\,dx
 +\int_{C_h}
   (I-\Pi_k)(K_h\rho_h g)\,
   (I-\Pi_k)(r+\pi_Qt_\vartheta)\,dx.
\]
Thus the first-order pilot error cancels and only a product of projection remainders survives.  The remaining unproved step is to derive, for the particular normalized splines and the spectrally stabilized random matrix, the uniform H\"older approximation constants, the claimed exponential inequality for the nondegenerate and degenerate Hoeffding components, and the simultaneous Gaussian perturbation bound.  Those facts are not statements in the frozen core and cannot be replaced by the definitions of \(B,S,G\).

\[
 E_Q=\left\{\left|\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)-\tau_Q(x_0)\right|
 \le R_n(h,k)\right\}.
\]
Then \(\Pr_Q(E_Q)\ge1-\eta\).  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}pointwise\text{-}identification}\), \(\tau_Q(x_0)=\tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\); by \(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}outcomes}\), this common value lies in \([-1,1]\).  Hence \(E_Q\) implies \(\tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\in C_n(h,k)\), even after intersection with \([-1,1]\).  Taking probabilities and then the infimum over \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\) gives the advertised coverage.  Privacy is already established by \(\mathrm{lem{:}private\text{-}release\text{-}and\text{-}sensitivity}\).  This completes the deterministic reduction, but it cannot establish unconditional coverage until the uniform-remainder target is proved.
